html:
The Pacahuara are a Panoan-speaking people of the northern Bolivian Amazon, in the Beni and Pando regions. Once a larger people, they now number only a handful, living in Tujuré on the Alto Ivón River beside the Chácobo.

They lived by hunting, fishing and farming along the rivers. Missionaries tried to gather them in the 1700s. The rubber boom of the late 1800s brought slave raids and disease that destroyed most of them. Their language is close to extinction. Neighbours included the Tacana and the Ese Ejja in Bolivia.
